changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 6 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/3880-es-done-listo.md`

- names `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx` → `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `Hecho` moved to the 3:1 majority `Listo`, which is the value objectui#3546 slice seven had already chosen for `common.done`. `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx` pinned the old outlier as a recorded example of deliberate divergence; that pin now asserts the four as one value instead, and its note keeps the history plus the `Pending`/zh row, which remains a genuine deliberate split.

### `.changeset/7313-object-calendar-record-source.md`

- names `plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `ObjectCalendar` resolves its records through the shared ladder (`resolveRecordSourceConfig` in `@object-ui/core`, called from `plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx`): `data` first, then `staticData`, then `objectName`. The published TypeScript interface REQUIRED `objectName` and declared neither `data` nor `staticData`; the published Zod mirror did the same. So an `object-calendar` node authored on `staticData` — the route the plugin page documents twice — rendered correctly and was refused by `safeValidateSchema`, and could not be annotated with its own type (`TS2741: Property 'objectName' is missing`).

### `.changeset/7712-kanban-calendar-filter-input.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `ObjectKanban.tsx` sends the authored key to the query as `$filter: schema.filter` and `ObjectCalendar.tsx` does the same, and `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap` declares `filter` on both blocks (measured: `safeParse` accepts it, and refuses an undeclared key by name on the same call). But none of the four registrations that publish those two renderers listed `filter` in `inputs`, and `sdui-parser`'s `validateTree` reports `unknown-prop` for every key no `inputs` entry claims. So an author writing the one spelling that WORKS was told it was unknown — objectui#6678's shape, where a correct write draws the same diagnostic as a write that does nothing. That is worse than an inert key: it actively punishes the correct behaviour, and the honest response to it is to delete working metadata.

### `.changeset/8171-calendar-sort-input.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#7712's defect, one key over. `ObjectCalendar.tsx` lowers the authored key onto its own query as `$orderby: convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)`, and `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap['object-calendar']` declares `sort` (measured on 17.2.0: `safeParse({ objectName, sort })` returns `success: true`, while the same strict schema on the same call refuses `bogusProp` by name — that control is what makes the acceptance a verdict). But neither of the two registrations that publish this renderer — `plugin-calendar:object-calendar` and `view:calendar` — listed `sort` in `inputs`, and `sdui-parser`'s `validateTree` reports `unknown-prop` for every key no `inputs` entry claims. So an author writing the one spelling that WORKS was told it was unknown — objectui#6678's shape, where a correct write draws the same diagnostic as a write that does nothing.

### `.changeset/8174-kanban-calendar-filter-sort.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `filter` had four declaration faces and only three of them named it: `@objectstack/spec` declares it (`ComponentPropsMap['object-kanban']` and `['object-calendar']`), both plugins' registration `inputs` publish it, and both renderers read it — `ObjectKanban.tsx` lowers `schema.filter` onto `$filter`, `ObjectCalendar.tsx` lowers `schema.filter` onto `$filter` and `schema.sort` onto `$orderby` through `convertSortToQueryParams`. This package's own published faces (the TypeScript interface and its zod mirror) named none of them, so an authored value reached the renderer only through `BaseSchema`'s index signature and the mirror's `.passthrough()` — admitted, never examined. That is the same reasoning objectstack-ai/objectui#7322 used to move `groupBy` and `limit` into this same interface.

### `.changeset/8466-calendar-color-allday-fields.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `ObjectCalendar.tsx`'s `getCalendarConfig` reads FIVE flat keys off the node, and `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` teaches all five in one sentence — "point `titleField` / `startDateField` / `endDateField` / `allDayField` / `colorField` at your own fields when they differ." Only three of the five were declared. The other two reached the renderer through `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any` on the TypeScript face and its `.passthrough()` on the zod mirror: admitted, never examined. A misspelling therefore left the calendar silently colourless while every published gate passed.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `f9d772b16` (merge-base with origin/main): 10 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1540 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2126 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36186180275)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `69b15589fa7cafaf52861d3c6cbd37b0e661fee6`

Read: card objectui#10668 (body and all three comments), the triage `5837671436`, the claim `5837748706`, the cited rulings objectui#10442 (body, triage, claim, ACCEPT, landed) with PR objectui#10561, objectui#10331 and objectui#10232, PR objectui#10711's file list (the objectui#10684 region partner), the PR body and file list, three check-run polls, `AGENTS.md` (changeset rule at line 168 and 版本号策略 at lines 267 to 272), `.changeset/config.json`, the header of `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, and the code by git only: `refs/review/pr-10717` at `69b15589f`, `refs/review/main` at `f9d772b16`, merge-base `383a34f529f6c60d3da4c1b76b502635f89a8b8d`. Diff: 14 files, +652 / −23, 7 commits (5 content, 2 merges of `origin/main`). The `os-dev-report` was not used as evidence; every reading below is off the diff and the head tree. Zero GitHub writes.

### ① Derived judgments

**Site 1, `packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx` (the card's face 1).** RIGHT.
- `GanttView.tsx:39` imports `useDisplayLocale` from `@object-ui/i18n`; `:878` now destructures only `t` from `useGanttTranslation()`; `:883` `const dateLocale = useDisplayLocale();` replaces `language || undefined`. No fallback added; the hook's own last resort (`useDisplayLocale.ts:71`, `locale || language || 'en'`) is the only one. This is the objectui#10442 shape the card asks for verbatim: 「each face formats with `useDisplayLocale()`. ⛔ Not the UI language, and not a machine-locale fallback.」
- `dateLocale` reaches, at the head: the header unit labels `:2050`, `:2052`, `:2054`; the band labels `:2278`, `:2306`; the toolbar period via `formatPeriodLabel` at `:2446` (`:444` to `:450`); the task list's compact row dates `:3893` and its Start / End cells `:3915`, `:3928`; the bar hover card `:4217`, `:4219`; the drag readouts `:4437`, `:4439` (summary chip) and `:4752` (bar overlay). The memo dependency lists at `:2071`, `:2314`, `:2447` already carried `dateLocale`, so no stale memo.
- Left alone and rightly so: the four `'en-CA'` ISO formatters at `:3821`, `:3822`, `:5025`, `:5026` (they seed the inline editor's date input, not a face) and `tzOffsetMs`'s `'en-US'` parser at `:299`. All three are declared `deliberate fallback` rows in `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts:288` to `:310`, with counts 2 / 2 / 1 that still match the head.
- `GanttView` declares no `locale` prop, so nothing authored can win here; the PR's statement to that effect is right. `@object-ui/i18n` was already a dependency (`packages/plugin-gantt/package.json:37`): no new edge.

**Site 2, `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` (the card's face 2).** RIGHT.
- `ObjectCalendar.tsx:29` imports the hook; `:354` `const displayLocale = useDisplayLocale();` and `:355` `const dialogLocale = locale !== undefined && locale !== 'default' ? locale : displayLocale;`, read directly under the existing `const { t } = useObjectTranslation();` at `:348`. The dialog's two calls are `:1454` `toLocaleDateString(dialogLocale, …)` and `:1456` `toLocaleTimeString(dialogLocale, …)`.
- Matches the grid: `CalendarView.tsx:167` defaults the prop to `"default"` and `:185` computes `effectiveLocale = locale !== "default" ? locale : displayLocale` (with `:184` `useDisplayLocale()`). `ObjectCalendar` forwards `locale={locale}` unchanged at `:1354`, so an undefined prop becomes the grid's `"default"`. Truth table, dialog vs grid: unset ⇒ display locale / display locale; `"default"` ⇒ display / display; a set tag ⇒ that tag / that tag. So a SET authored `locale` still wins where it did before, exactly as the ruling permits (「An authored `locale` that is set may still win where it did before; say so where it does」), and the changeset says so.
- No back door upstream: `calendar-view-renderer.tsx:137` to `:145` `resolveAuthoredLocale` returns `undefined` for anything but a string `Intl` accepts, and `index.tsx:261` does the same, so neither boundary ever hands the UI language in as the `locale` prop.
- Region partition (claim: 「⛔ Not a data view's fetch effect, rows commit or `loading` release」): the three hunks sit at `:26` to `:29`, `:346` to `:355` and `:1451` to `:1457`. The fetch effect is `:604` to `:800`; the `loading` state at `:361` and its releases at `:629`, `:692`, `:789`, `:794` are untouched. PR objectui#10711 (objectui#10684) edits `RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx`, `ReportView.tsx`, `record-reference-rail.tsx`, `ObjectTimeline.tsx` and three changesets: zero file overlap with this PR.
- The prop surface is unchanged: `locale?: string` at `:173`, no new prop.

**Sites 3 and 4, `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/HomeRail.tsx` and `packages/app-shell/src/layout/InboxPopover.tsx` (found by the census).** IN SCOPE, and RIGHT.
- Is a relative-time face a "date face" in the triage's sense? The repo already answered: objectui#10331's table names `MarketplacePage`'s `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(language || 'en')` as one of three console faces that 「format dates in the UI language rather than the display locale」, and objectui#10232 §2 names `StudioHomePage`'s `relativeTime` (`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`) under the same `useDisplayLocale.ts` contract, 「Every date, number and currency renderer goes through here」. Both landed on the hook: `MarketplacePage.tsx:58` / `:66`, `StudioHomePage.tsx:152` / `:433`. `timeAgo` (`utils/relativeTime.ts:20` to `:25`) is `formatRelativeTime` (`packages/i18n/src/utils/formatting.ts:97`, `new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, …)`). So these two are the class the triage told the census to find (「census the date faces for any other read that is not `useDisplayLocale()`」) and the claim's own surface (「plus any other date face the census finds that does not read `useDisplayLocale()`」). Not a scope breach; neither file is held.
- `HomeRail.tsx:19` swaps the import to `useDisplayLocale` (the file took only `language` from `useObjectTranslation`; `t` is a `TFn` prop); `:150` and `:266` read the hook in `HomeActionCenter` and `HomeActivity`; `:213` and `:280` pass `displayLocale` to `timeAgo`. Both calls checked.
- `InboxPopover.tsx:36` adds the import, keeps `useObjectTranslation` for `t` at `:73`; `:76` reads the hook; `:236` (row), `:447` (group's `latestCreatedAt`), `:559` (activity) pass `displayLocale`. All three calls checked; at the head every `timeAgo(` caller in `packages/` passes `displayLocale` (five sites, none other).
- The two other `formatRelativeTime` names at the head (`ActivityFeed.tsx:92`, `RecordMetaFooter.tsx:77`) are local helpers that take `t` and use no `Intl`; rightly not touched.
